write_up: You're a Marketing Coordinator in B2B software, with earlier marketing work at Keystone Benefits Group. Your resume is relevant to Tallgrass, but it's common for coordinator resumes to list recurring duties without showing what went into them. In a pile, that makes it difficult to distinguish your work from someone else's, especially for a job centered on marketing systems.

The content calendar line is the strongest model: it names what you managed and the two channels it served. Your skills list also names the three tools Tallgrass asks for, but it sits apart from the work, so a recruiter can't tell which tasks you did in each one.

Let's start with Brightfield's newsletter and webinar lines. Add your part and the details you can substantiate, then connect your reporting and campaign work to the tools you used. Leave the calendar line's named channels in place.

cards.line: - Coordinated the monthly customer newsletter and product announcement emails
cards.cannot_tell: Coordinated could mean several different jobs. A recruiter can't tell what you handled or how many people received the newsletter.
cards.example: Coordinated the monthly customer newsletter and product announcement emails, handling [your tasks] for [audience size]
cards.question: What parts of the emails did you handle, and how many people received them?

cards.line: - Supported webinar planning with the product marketing team
cards.cannot_tell: The product marketing team is named, but your part in planning isn't. Tallgrass wants webinar support from registration through follow-up, so the steps you handled matter here.
cards.example: Supported webinar planning with the product marketing team by [your tasks] for [webinar topic]
cards.question: What did you handle for a webinar, and what was it about?

cards.line: - Managed the content calendar for LinkedIn and the company blog
cards.cannot_tell: Keep this as a model: it pairs your responsibility with the places the work appeared. Use that same approach to name the deliverables in your other lines.

cards.line: - Pulled weekly campaign reports for the marketing manager
cards.cannot_tell: A recruiter can see who received the reports, but not what they measured or which tools you used. Those details matter for a role with HubSpot and Google Analytics 4 reporting.
cards.example: Pulled weekly campaign reports on [metrics] for the marketing manager using [tool]
cards.question: Which metrics did the reports cover, and what did you use to pull them?

cards.line: - Helped prepare slide decks and one-pagers for the sales team
cards.cannot_tell: The deliverables are clear, but helped leaves your part open. A subject or example would show what you contributed to the sales materials.
cards.example: Helped prepare slide decks and one-pagers for the sales team by [your contribution] on [subject]
cards.question: What did you contribute to the materials, and what did they cover?

cards.line: - Kept the brand asset library organized
cards.cannot_tell: The library is named, but the work behind keeping it organized isn't. A recruiter can't tell what you maintained or how the sales and marketing teams used it.
cards.example: Kept the brand asset library organized by [your method] for [users]
cards.question: How did you maintain the library, and who used it?
